sources.title: MIVUBI Effects Attributes and Component Mutation Policy v1

facts.subject: effect and attribute baseline
facts.statement: Each arena/player/entity role must declare a baseline contract for status effects, health/max-health, movement-related attributes, combat modifiers, component groups, and project properties that should hold before gameplay starts and after reset completes.

facts.subject: temporary effect ownership
facts.statement: Temporary effects and modifiers should be owned by a scoped source with arenaGeneration, lifeGeneration or entityGeneration, effectGeneration, and reason so cleanup can remove or reconcile only the ending scope.

facts.subject: health attribute mutation
facts.statement: Any max-health change must define current-health reconciliation semantics, including whether current health clamps, preserves ratio, resets to max, or remains unchanged; do not infer one behavior implicitly.

facts.subject: component group activation
facts.statement: Project-triggered component-group changes should be generation-aware and idempotent. Re-adding an already-active group is not automatically harmless because stateful components may reinitialize.

facts.subject: event-driven component mutation
facts.statement: After entity events that modify properties or component groups, downstream logic must treat the mutation as queued until post-tick verification confirms the expected state. Same-tick reads are not commit proof.

facts.subject: attribute and effect authority
facts.statement: For each logical modifier such as speed boost, damage buff, resistance, downed slow, or revive immunity, declare one gameplay authority; status effect, property, component group, equipment modifier, and scoreboard mirrors must not independently decide the same state.

facts.subject: arena reset
facts.statement: Arena cleanup must reconcile all ending-generation effects, attribute overrides, component groups, temporary properties, fire/state modifiers, and equipment-derived gameplay modifiers before declaring player/entity normal form.

facts.subject: respawn and revive
facts.statement: Respawn and revive flows must explicitly define which effects and component groups are cleared, preserved, or reapplied. Health restoration alone does not constitute a complete life-state reset.

facts.subject: stacked temporary modifiers
facts.statement: When multiple systems can apply semantically similar buffs or debuffs, track owner sets or a resolved effective modifier instead of blindly applying/removing effects; removing one owner must not erase another valid owner's contribution.

facts.subject: post-reset verification
facts.statement: VERIFY_EMPTY or player normal-form checks should include absence/presence of expected status effects, current/max health relationship, active project properties, and component-group-derived behavior indicators where observable.
